contests.exchange: RST + serial; island stations add IOTA reference
contests.source_note: RSGB rules 2026, rule 2: 'the contest always takes place over the last FULL weekend of July'. Verified 2026-08-11.

contests.name: ARS Spartan Sprint
contests.exchange: RST + state/province + power output
contests.note: CORRECTION: previously encoded as the first TUESDAY of the month. The sponsor's rule is the first MONDAY US local, which lands on Tuesday UTC -- and those are different dates whenever the 1st falls on a Tuesday (Sep and Dec 2026). Now anchored on the first Monday with a +1 day offset. LOCAL-TIME CONTEST: ARS gives no UTC time and states the event does not shift for DST, so the UTC time is what moves: 0100-0300 UTC Tuesday under US standard time, 0000-0200 UTC Tuesday under US daylight time. Stored value is the standard-time rendering; resolve per-season when the local-time engine gap is closed.
contests.source_note: ars-qrp.com Spartan Sprint page: 'Held on the first Monday of every month', 'EASTERN 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. Local. CENTRAL 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Local MOUNTAIN 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Local PACIFIC 5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. Local', '(Does not shift for DST - This event is always at these Local Times)', 'a simple, casual 2 Hour QRP CW Event', 'open to all QRP CW operators - there is no membership requirement'.

eligibility.note: ars-qrp.com: 'It is open to all QRP CW operators - there is no membership requirement.'

contests.summary: Monthly two-hour QRP CW sprint on the first Monday evening. Scoring rewards a low station weight as well as QSOs, which is what makes it distinctive.

contests.summary: Weekly one-hour high-speed CW sprints, typically 25-40+ wpm. Four sessions per week give worldwide coverage across all time zones.

contests.source_note: ncjweb.com/Sprint-Rules.pdf, 'Rules: 2026 North American Sprint (CW/RTTY)', rule 4 Contest Periods: 'CW: 0000 until 0359 UTC, February 8, 2026' and, under 'September Contests (NOTE CW DATE SHIFT)', 'CW: 0000 until 0359 UTC, September 13, 2026'. contests.name: 4 States QRP Group Second Sunday Sprint (SSS)
contests.exchange: RST + state/province/country + 4SQRP member number (power if non-member)
contests.source_note: 4sqrp.com SSS rules (revised 02/2026), TIME/DATE: 'The SSS is held the second Sunday night of every month (local time). It runs for two (2) hours from 7 PM until 9 PM central time (CST or CDT, whichever is in effect at the time). If you use UTC, that time changes when we switch from CST to CDT (or vice versa).' Power: 'CW & Digital: 5 Watts or less; SSB: 10 Watts PEP or less.'
contests.note: LOCAL-TIME CONTEST. The anchor is the second SUNDAY, but the sprint runs into Monday UTC. Stored UTC is the CST rendering, 0100-0300 UTC Monday. Under CDT the sponsor states the UTC time shifts an hour earlier, to 0000-0200 UTC Monday -- the sponsor says so explicitly. Resolve per-season when the local-time engine gap is closed.
contests.summary: Monthly two-hour QRP sprint on the second Sunday evening US Central time. CW, SSB and digital all count; the CW/SSB power limits differ, so operators switching modes must change power.

eligibility.note: 4SQRP rules: 'Anyone can participate'. Non-member QSOs count for one point provided the non-member is also running QRP power.

contests.name: PODXS 070 Club PSKfest
contests.exchange: State/province/country (SPC)
contests.source_note: podxs070.com PSKfest rules, DATE: '0000-2359 UTC On the 1st Saturday following January 1st'. BANDS: '80 thru 10 meters, no WARC bands'. Cross-checked against the club's own 'Contest Calendar' page, which states each recurrence rule in words AND publishes a projected date table for 2026-2035. Both agree. The club's table gives 8-Jan-28 and 8-Jan-33 -- both years in which January 1 is itself a Saturday -- confirming 'following January 1st' excludes January 1.
contests.summary: The club's flagship 24-hour PSK31 party and the first PSK contest of the year.

eligibility.note: PSKfest's own page states no entrant clause, unlike most other 070 contests. The club's general rules impose no membership requirement and the SPC exchange is open to anyone, so worldwide is the strong reading -- but it is a reading, not a quote.

Cross-checked against the club's own 'Contest Calendar' page, which states each recurrence rule in words AND publishes a projected date table for 2026-2035. Both agree.
contests.note: The 0000-2359 window is the sprint's outer bound, not its length: 'For scoring, your six hour block will begin with the hour that you select on the scorer page and continue for the next 6 hours.' Maximum operating time is six hours.
contests.summary: PSK31 sprint scoring YL contacts double. Operators enter an OM or YL category and pick any six-hour block in the UTC day.

eligibility.note: podxs070.com: 'This event is open to all amateur radio operators licensed to operate on the HF bands.'

contests.name: PODXS 070 Club Three Day Weekend (TDW)
contests.exchange: Members: 070 Club number. Non-members: 0000 in place of a club number.
contests.source_note: podxs070.com TDW rules, Dates: 'First Weekend ending in June'; Time: '0000 UTC Friday - 2359 UTC Sunday'. Cross-checked against the club's own 'Contest Calendar' page, which states each recurrence rule in words AND publishes a projected date table for 2026-2035. Both agree.
contests.note: 'First weekend ENDING in June' is why this anchors on the first SUNDAY of June and counts backwards to the Friday, rather than anchoring on a Friday in June. The club's own table proves the distinction matters: it lists 31-May-30 and 30-May-31, where the contest starts in May.
contests.summary: 72-hour PSK31 event over the first weekend that ends in June, with bonus stations to hunt.

eligibility.note: podxs070.com: 'This event is open to all amateur radio operators licensed to operate on the HF bands.'

eligibility.note: This contest's AGCW page states no entrant clause. AGCW's other contests say 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure' and nothing here restricts entry, so worldwide is the strong reading -- but it is a reading, not a quote.

contests.name: AGCW Handtastenparty 40m (HTP)
contests.exchange: RST + running 3-digit QSO number from 001 + class + name + age
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/htp: 'Handtastenparty 40m: Jährlich am ersten Samstag im September vom 13:00 bis 16:00 UTC, nächster Termin: 5. September 2026'.
contests.summary: The 40 m running of the straight-key party, three hours on the first Saturday of September.

eligibility.note: This contest's AGCW page states no entrant clause. AGCW's other contests say 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure' and nothing here restricts entry, so worldwide is the strong reading -- but it is a reading, not a quote.

contests.name: Deutscher Telegrafie Contest (DTC)
contests.exchange: German stations: RST + LDK (district vehicle registration code). All others: RST only.
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/dtc: 'Seit einigen Jahren findet er stets am Tag der Deutschen Einheit (3. Oktober) von 07:00–10:00 UTC (09:00–12:00 Uhr MESZ) auf den Bändern 80m und 40m statt.' Run jointly with the High Speed Club since 1971.
contests.note: Anchored on German Unity Day, a fixed calendar date, so it moves through the week rather than sitting on a weekend. 'Seit einigen Jahren' -- for some years now -- is AGCW hedging its own history, not the current rule.
contests.summary: Three-hour hand-copy CW contest on German Unity Day. Electronic decoders are explicitly disqualifying.

eligibility.practical: Every QSO must involve a German station: 'Mindestens eine der an einem QSO beteiligten Stationen muss sich in Deutschland befinden.' Non-DL entrants can therefore work only DL stations.
eligibility.note: agcw.de: 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateurinnen und Funamateure (nur Single-OP).' Entry is open worldwide; the DL requirement constrains who you can work, not who may enter.

contests.name: AGCW QRP/QRP Party
contests.exchange: RST + running number + class
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/qrp-qrp: 'Termin: Jährlich am 1. Mai von 1300 bis 1900 UTC.' Ziel: 'Förderung des Betriebs mit geringer Sendeleistung. Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure und SWL.'
contests.summary: Six-hour QRP-to-QRP party on May 1st -- both ends of every QSO are meant to be running low power.

eligibility.note: agcw.de: 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure und SWL.'

contests.name: AGCW Schlackertastenabend (STA)
contests.exchange: RST + running QSO number from 001 per year + type of bug used
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/sta: 'Termin: Jeden dritten Mittwoch im Februar und jeden dritten Mittwoch im Oktober von 1900 bis 2030 UTC. Nächster Termin: 21. Okt. 2026'.
contests.note: AGCW's own 'nächster Termin: 21. Okt. 2026' is the independent check on the October leg -- the third Wednesday of October 2026 is indeed the 21st.
contests.summary: Semi-automatic key ('bug') evening, 90 minutes twice a year. Entrants report which bug they used.

eligibility.note: This contest's AGCW page states no entrant clause. AGCW's other contests say 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure' and nothing here restricts entry, so worldwide is the strong reading -- but it is a reading, not a quote.

contests.name: AGCW VHF/UHF Contest
contests.exchange: RST + running number + locator
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/vhf-uhf: 'Termine: Jährlich 1. Januar, 3. Samstag im März, 2. Samstag im Juni, 4. Samstag im September, jeweils auf den Bändern 2m/70cm: VHF von 14.00 bis 17.00 UTC auf 2m (144 MHz) und UHF von 17.00 bis 18.00 UTC auf 70cm (432 MHz).'
contests.note: Four dates a year, each with two back-to-back sessions on different bands: the first session is 2 m only, the second 70 cm only. Encoded as two sessions off one anchor, so eight occurrences a year. The per-session band split is not expressible in the current schema -- both bands are listed at contest level.
contests.summary: AGCW's CW-only VHF/UHF activity contest: three hours on 2 m followed immediately by one hour on 70 cm, four times a year.

eligibility.note: agcw.de: 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure.'

contests.name: AGCW YL-CW-Party
contests.exchange: RST + running QSO number from 001 + 'YL' or 'OM' + first name
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/yl-cw-party: 'Am ersten Dienstag im März findet die YL-CW-Party statt, zu der auch alle OMs und SWLs herzlich eingeladen sind. Nächster Termin: 3. März 2026.' Zeiten: '19:00 - 21:00 UTC (20:00 - 22:00 MEZ)'.
contests.note: AGCW's own 'Nächster Termin: 3. März 2026' is the independent check -- the first Tuesday of March 2026 is the 3rd. OM-to-OM QSOs score zero, so the contest is built around working YLs.
contests.summary: Two-hour 80 m party centred on YL operators. OMs and SWLs are invited, but OM-to-OM contacts score nothing.

eligibility.note: agcw.de: the party is one 'zu der auch alle OMs und SWLs herzlich eingeladen sind' -- OMs and SWLs are expressly invited alongside YLs.

contests.name: AGCW ZAP Merit Contest (ZMC)
contests.exchange: Callsign + date + time + RST (SWLs log RST of both stations in a QSO)
contests.source_note: agcw.de/contest/tzap: 'Termin: jeden Montag, Vorloggen ab 1740 UTC, Telegrammsendung 1800 UTC.' Ziel: 'Hören und Bestätigen von Telegrammsendungen auf 3.563 kHz (80m-Band). Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure und SWLs.'
contests.note: PARTLY UNVERIFIED. The recurrence (every Monday), the 1740 UTC pre-logging opening and the 1800 UTC telegram transmission are all quoted from AGCW. AGCW publishes NO closing time. The 1830 end stored here is a PLACEHOLDER so the record expands -- it is not a sponsor fact and must not be presented as one. Confirm the session length with the ZMC manager before shipping. Points accumulate over a calendar year; logs are due 31 January of the following year.
contests.summary: Weekly Monday-evening telegram-copying activity on 3.563 kHz, scored as a year-long merit tally rather than a single contest.

eligibility.note: agcw.de: 'Teilnehmen können alle Funkamateure und SWLs.'
